subject: Tight SLO synthesis & next steps — Vertex Health deployment
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@vertexhealth.com>, Alex Morales <alex.morales@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Tight SLO synthesis & next steps — Vertex Health deployment

Hi Jane / Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick synthesis of what we heard on the call and proposed next steps so everyone has the same reference.

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary goal: PVH (patient-facing) triage and templating flows with sub-250ms p95 inference for typical prompts once warm. You emphasized low tail latency for clinician experience.
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~120 req/s across business hours, with predictable scheduled spikes (up to ~450–600 req/s) during batch intake windows.
- Typical prompt size: 40–120 tokens (most ~64 tokens). Many prompts reuse similar prefixes — opportunity for prefix/KV caching.
- Model: you want an open model variant (13B-ish) but with high-quality responses; you mentioned interest in 8-bit/quantized variants if latency/cost are significantly better without degrading output.
- Deployment: private VPC deployment preferred for PHI; SOC 2 + auditability required. Initial pilot target: Q4 (6–10 week technical pilot).

Technical constraints that matter
- P95 SLO target: aim for <=250ms for 64-token median prompts post-cache warm (you asked for baseline numbers for different token lengths).
- Cold-starts: you expect a small number of cold sessions during off-hours; fallback model/region routing must be explicit.
- Cost sensitivity: target to keep per-1k-token inference cost below your internal threshold (you provided a ballpark on the call).

Our immediate deliverables
1) Sizing matrix (attached: vertex_sla_matrix.xlsx) — baseline GPU counts, batching, and quantization options mapped to your traffic buckets.
2) Deployment topology draft (attached: redwood-deploy-topology-v1.pdf) — VPC layout, KMS integration, audit log flow.
3) Latency sim results (attached: kv-cache-latency-sim.csv) — quick KV-cache sim we ran with representative prompt shapes.
4) Security pack: SOC2 summary + questions we need answered about your egress policy (we'll share in a separate drive link).

Proposed next steps
- You: share an anonymized sample of typical prompts (no PHI) we can use for realistic sims (Jane: if you can get this by next Wed that helps).
- Us: Jonas will schedule a 90-minute deep technical session (infra + security + ML infra) — propose Tue 21 Jul or Wed 22 Jul.
- Us: provide a short-run performance test in our staging VPC (no PHI) within two weeks after we have the sample prompts.

If anything above is off, tell me and I'll update. Otherwise I'll assume we move forward with the plan above and will follow up with calendar invites and an updated HubSpot timeline.

Thanks —

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vertex_sla_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-deploy-topology-v1.pdf (diagram), kv-cache-latency-sim.csv (CSV)

Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 18:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tight SLO synthesis & next steps — Vertex Health deployment

Sofia —

Thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side:
- Our internal p95 target is more aggressive in the clinician path: 200–220ms for ~64 tokens (post-warm). If achieving <=250ms is the realistic first milestone, that works as a staged target but please call out what changes are required to hit ~200ms.
- Peak: during nightly intake we can see short bursts up to ~600 req/s for ~10–15 minutes; sustained spikes usually top ~450 req/s.
- Model preference: we are open to an LLaMA-2-style 13B quantized variant, but we need a short AB test plan that compares 8-bit quantization vs bfloat16 runs for both latency and hallucination rate on our prompt set.
- Security: SOC 2 + HIPAA posture are table stakes. Please include sample audit logs and retention options in the security pack.

Timeline: Q4 pilot still looks right from our end but procurement wants a clear milestone list by end of July so they can budget.

Thanks — I'll try to send a sanitized prompt sample by Tue EOD.

—Jane
VP Product, Vertex Health
jane.sullivan@vertexhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0228

Subject: Internal: quick ops plan for Vertex Health pilot

Sofia / Karthik —

Quick internal checklist following Jane's clarification:
- Action: Run targeted latency sims for 64-token median and 32-token lower-tail with both 8-bit quantized and bfloat16. Owner: Jonas. ETA: 7 business days after prompt sample.
- Action: Prepare AB test harness (blind eval) that measures hallucination/regression on 120 labeled prompts. Owner: Karthik. ETA: 10 business days.
- Action: Provision staging VPC region us-west-2 with 3 x A100-equivalent nodes + 1 multi-tenant fallback pool for cold starts. Owner: Infra (I will open a ticket). ETA: 5 business days.
- Action: Produce SOC2 + audit log excerpt for procurement. Owner: Security (requesting a short pack we can redline).

Notes: For hitting the ~200ms p95 we should consider: 1) enabling persistent KV-cache for the clinician flow, 2) enabling smaller per-request batching (batch-size ceiling 8) to keep latency predictable, and 3) evaluate quantization + kernel selection (we may need to try int4 on one run to see the regression cost).

I'll log these in the HubSpot deal and tag the infra ticket.

Jonas
